title: Salesforce’s $25 Billion Buyback Is Looking Like A Great Deal. Cramer Says “Whatever Was Ailing The Stock Is Over”
detail:
Salesforce’s $25 Billion Buyback Is Looking Like A Great Deal. Cramer Says “Whatever Was Ailing The Stock Is Over”
AJ Tiarsmith
Wed, September 16, 2026 at 2:15 PM EDT 4 min read
CRM
Trade CRM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) repurchased shares at a ~$176 average through its $25 billion program; the stock now trades at $252, validating the timing.

CRM is down 5% year to date but has surged 28% over the past month, a tension Cramer's bullish framing does not fully address.

Slackbot hit one million active users five months post-launch, up 150% quarter over quarter, with Slack posting its fastest AOV growth since acquisition.

Read More: Learn 7 secret wealth tips high net worth investors use that most investors miss (sponsor)

Jim Cramer used his Mad Dash segment on Wednesday to make a bullish call on Salesforce (NYSE:CRM), arguing that the software giant's aggressive buyback is aging well and that sentiment around the name has turned. His summary line: "There's a lot of sense that whatever was ailing the stock is over." Cramer is describing a sentiment he detected around the company, not citing a specific metric.

24/7 Wall St.
CRM Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
Why Cramer Thinks the Buyback Looks Smart

Cramer's core argument was about timing. He told viewers Salesforce "bought a huge amount of stock back in the 170s, according to CNBC. That looks like it's a pretty smart deal. People felt that they were hurting their balance sheet. Well, it turns out it didn't even dent their balance sheet. It's a very positive story." The characterization of the balance sheet is Cramer's, not ours.

The program he is referring to has been reported at $25 billion in size, disclosed alongside the company's most recent quarterly results in the Q2 FY27 8-K exhibit filed on August 26, 2026. The Q2 release described an accelerated share repurchase with an average price of $176 per share to date and an expectation to "repurchase at least 14% of shares outstanding through this program."

Set Cramer's 170s against where Salesforce trades now: $251.59 as of 1:34 p.m. ET on September 16, 2026. Readers can draw their own conclusion about the entry point.

Salesforce (CRM) stock is back in focus after Dreamforce 2026, where the company emphasized Agentforce, introduced the new Koa reasoning model developed with Nvidia, and expanded AI-focused partnerships.

For investors, the headline at Dreamforce is how this AI story now links to Salesforce's chart. The share price is around $255.65, with a 30.3% 1 month share price return and a 64.9% 3 month share price return indicating strong recent momentum. By contrast, the 1 year total shareholder return of 7.7% and 5 year total shareholder return of 0.8% reflect a more muted longer track record as the market digests earnings, AI product launches and the rotation back into enterprise software.

Scan how the Salesforce AI story compares with other enterprise software names riding similar momentum by checking out the hand-picked 60 AI infrastructure stocks.

The AI rush has lifted Salesforce's share price rapidly, which leaves a simple fork in the road for investors: pay up after this spike, or wait and risk the train leaving without you as the valuation picture comes into focus next.

Most Popular Narrative: Fairly Valued

The market now prices Salesforce almost exactly where the most followed narrative pegs fair value, with the last close at $255.65 against a fair value of about $255.90. This puts the focus firmly on what could shift that balance rather than on any obvious valuation gap.

The per-seat licence was only ever the toll booth. The asset is the governed system of record: every customer, every deal, every entitlement, for about 80% of the Fortune 500. And the one thing an autonomous AI agent cannot do is act on a customer without getting into that record first. An agent with no permissions, no governance and no audit trail is not an asset, it is a liability waiting to happen. So the same automation wave that threatens the seat count is exactly what drives every serious enterprise deeper into the data layer Salesforce owns. The meter changes from per-person to per-action. It does not disappear.

See why 41 investors see Salesforce as 0% undervalued.

According to michaelyang, that shift toward usage based on actions helps explain why Salesforce is currently viewed as fairly priced on this narrative, with only a 0% discount to fair value and the investment debate now hinging more on execution and competitive pressure than on a clear mispricing.

Result: Fair Value of $255.90 (ABOUT RIGHT)

Still, this Salesforce narrative could break if AI agents fail to deliver meaningful usage or if Microsoft Copilot starts displacing Salesforce inside large enterprise accounts.

title: Jim Cramer calls Salesforce stock too cheap at Dreamforce 2026

Jim Cramer calls Salesforce stock too cheap at Dreamforce 2026
Jim Cramer calls Salesforce stock too cheap at Dreamforce 2026 · Quartz · Bloomberg / Getty Images
Cris Tolomia
Wed, September 16, 2026 at 1:11 PM EDT 2 min read
CRM
Trade CRM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Jim Cramer called Salesforce stock undervalued on Wednesday as the enterprise software company's annual Dreamforce conference continued, according to CNBC.

At a valuation of approximately 15 times forward earnings, Cramer declared Salesforce stock is "way too cheap" at the CNBC Investing Club's morning meeting. He expressed confidence that Salesforce has left behind the concerns about AI disruption that had previously pressured its share price. Salesforce stock fell 2% on Wednesday.

Cramer also defended the company's debt-fueled stock buyback from earlier this year, which had drawn criticism. "I always heard that people say they're going to wreck the balance sheet," he said. "Well, not only did they not wreck the balance sheet, it's got to be one of the greatest buybacks in history."

At the conference on Tuesday, Salesforce introduced AIForce, described as a live interface spanning its broader ecosystem, along with Koa, a newly developed reasoning model for Agentforce built through a collaboration with Nvidia.

Salesforce had been among a group of enterprise software stocks that came under sustained selling pressure as investors grew skeptical that traditional software models could remain competitive against the backdrop of accelerating AI development. Those declines were compounded by large short positions held by Situational Awareness, a leveraged hedge fund that had bet against software companies based on that thesis. When the fund was forced to unwind its trades in late July, those short positions became a tailwind for the stocks it had targeted.

Salesforce stock recovered in August after better-than-expected quarterly results quieted what Cramer called fears of a "SaaSpocalypse." Situational Awareness, which peaked at $45 billion in assets at the start of July, lost roughly $35 billion after margin calls from prime brokers Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase forced a distressed sale of its publicly traded holdings.

Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust holds a long position in Salesforce, according to CNBC.

title: Did Salesforce Telegraph Its Own Massive Rally?
detail:
Did Salesforce Telegraph Its Own Massive Rally?
Trefis Team
Wed, September 16, 2026 at 1:04 PM EDT 3 min read
ADBE
NOW
HUBS
MSFT
CRM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pexels

Salesforce (CRM) stock has run hard since June 15, 2026, and the easy explanation is the August 26, 2026 earnings call plus Claudeforce, a product built jointly with Anthropic and announced minutes before that call. That explanation arrives late. Management had outlined the turnaround metrics and projected timeline well in advance of the market repricing.

What Was Salesforce Saying Before The Run?

Go back to December 3, 2025. That day, the company disclosed that growth in net new Annual Contract Value (ACV)—defined as new bookings less attrition—outpaced overall ACV growth for the first time since fiscal 2022. Management noted that organic revenue re-acceleration historically follows this crossover. On the same call it committed to re-accelerating revenue in twelve to eighteen months. By February 25, 2026 the half was named: organic revenue re-acceleration in the second half of fiscal 2027.

Why Was Salesforce Buying Its Own Shares?

The second sign was where the cash went. On that February 25, 2026 call the company raised its repurchase authorization to $50 billion, calling its own share price dislocated and the buyback the most prudent investment available to it. It then commenced its largest ever accelerated share repurchase, $25 billion. On the May 27, 2026 call it said that program, with the ongoing buyback, had cut first-quarter diluted share count 10% year over year. The balance sheet was being put behind the forecast. The run did not begin until June 15, 2026, with the stock at $164.55.

What Landed On The August Call?

Then the checkpoint, on August 26, 2026. Current remaining performance obligation grew 14% in constant currency, a point ahead of the company's own guide, against approximately 13% in constant currency on the May 27, 2026 call. Management calls it a leading indicator. Net new ACV growth was the strongest in four years, and attrition was near its lowest level ever. Management also answered the predicted end of software, saying none of those predictions had come true for Salesforce. The joint product announced that day was not a surprise either. In May, management had already said that Anthropic's own Sales Cloud usage had exploded fivefold on the back of Headless 360, launched that April, which made all of Salesforce reachable by outside software.

Could You Have Acted On Salesforce's Own Guidance?

The indicators were present, but guidance carries execution risk. The re-acceleration management promised is for the second half of fiscal 2027, and it has not been reported yet. What the market repriced by September 15, 2026 was confidence in that commitment, not the commitment being met. Over the run since June 15, 2026 the stock returned +55.4%, while the S&P 500 returned +0.7%, Microsoft (MSFT) returned +24.6%, Oracle (ORCL) returned -26.9% and Adobe (ADBE) returned +24.9%. So software did not move as a block, and Salesforce more than doubled the best of these peers. Timing stayed the hard part. Ten days before the run began, on June 5, 2026, implied volatility sat in the 85th percentile of its trailing one-year range, which signaled a large move in either direction, not which one. The repeatable habit is to watch companies whose own outlook is climbing while the price still lags.
